intro: The ship was crushed by pack ice in the first winter, and the wreck is still out there somewhere under the floes. What survives of the expedition is a biscuit tin full of messages, each written in a different hand, and each deliberately obscure. At base camp the survivors pass the dark hours mending harnesses, scraping snow-lamps, and reading the tin aloud in turn, as if the writers might still be listening at the edge of the tent. The tin's lid carries a little hasp meant for as many seals as there are hands, and it will not lift unless all are pressed down together. Outside, the wind hums through the guy-ropes, and nobody speaks of going home.
echo: For three days nobody could see the next tent.

puzzles.title: Nunatak

blocks.text: The knight sets out from d3: Nb4 Na2 Nc1 Nb3 Na1 Nc2 Ne1.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there?

puzzles.title: Midnight Sun
puzzles.flavor: Up and down, up and down, and not a single space left.

blocks.text: NDPEY TTSSE ZJOOH OEOOY XETDN OEOET IFROH PIESU TNWRT EMMTR BECAN GHATR ISEDR E

hints: All the right letters are here, just out of order. Could they have been written along a path that goes up and down?

puzzles.title: Frost Smoke
puzzles.flavor: Lord Playfair's friend got the credit, but the square is built from whatever is written above it.

blocks.text: SI MP HA OZ SI DU IO GA EX KO BS SO SZ XG IK MO SO BO GA UC PK XK UR GK KH YK TF LP NK EY

hints: An even number of letters, read in pairs, and no pair is ever a double. Which cipher works on pairs, and where's its key?

puzzles.title: Farthest South
puzzles.flavor: Half a ladder, read from the far end.
hints: This is DNA, but not the strand a cell would read. What is its partner, and which end does reading start from?

puzzles.title: Katabatic
puzzles.flavor: The typist's hands were fine. Their aim was not.
hints: Every letter is close to the right one. Close on what? Look down at your hands.

meta.title: Meta: The Last Expedition
meta.flavor: Every report is signed with a single initial. Blaise would know what to do with them.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
